skill.name: c4-container
skill.description: Expert C4 Container-level documentation specialist. Synthesizes Component-level documentation into Container-level architecture, mapping components to deployment units, documenting container interfaces as APIs, and creating container diagrams. Use when synthesizing components into deployment containers and documenting system deployment architecture.
skill.summary: Synthesize component documentation into C4 container architecture outputs.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, diagram fences, and placeholder API documentation. No evidence of command execution, unauthorized network activity, prompt injection, or system reconnaissance intent was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.
- Mermaid container diagrams showing deployment architecture

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks mark an inline Markdown filename reference to a local resource. This is documentation text, not shell or Ruby execution.
The backticks format an example HTTP endpoint in documentation. There is no executable command or instruction to run it.
The backticks format an example POST endpoint in an API template. This is not shell syntax or dynamic command execution.
The flagged text starts a Mermaid code fence for a C4 diagram example. It documents diagram syntax and does not execute commands.
The snippet is a Markdown fence terminator after a diagram example. It has no runtime behavior or command execution path.
The four-backtick fence separates documentation sections. It is Markdown structure, not an instruction to invoke a shell.
The flagged fence closes a quoted documentation block. No command, interpreter, or user-controlled execution is present.
The fenced block is a YAML OpenAPI template for documentation. It is not code that the skill executes.
The URL points to c4model.com as a cited documentation source. The skill does not instruct the agent to send data there.
The URL is a placeholder server in an OpenAPI example. It is not used for network access or data transfer.
The line introduces Mermaid C4Container syntax for architecture documentation. It does not request host, network, or environment reconnaissance.
The snippet begins a Mermaid diagram fence. It contains static architecture examples, not system probing behavior.
The line describes expected diagram output for deployment architecture. It does not instruct collection of local system details.

content.value_statement: Container architecture documentation can become inconsistent when components, APIs, and deployment units are tracked separately. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code synthesize components into C4 container documents, diagrams, and API summaries.
actual_capabilities: Synthesizes component documentation into C4 container-level architecture descriptions.
Maps components to deployment containers and records deployment rationale.
Documents container interfaces, protocols, endpoints, and dependencies.
Creates Mermaid C4Container diagram guidance for system deployment views.
Provides OpenAPI and Swagger template guidance for container APIs.
Highlights infrastructure, scaling, and deployment configuration details.
limitations: It depends on accurate component, deployment, and interface inputs.
It does not automatically inspect source code or live infrastructure.
It provides documentation templates, not validated OpenAPI files.
It is not a substitute for security, reliability, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Prepare service documentation
use_cases.description: Turn component notes into clear container documentation for service ownership and onboarding.

use_cases.title: Create API architecture notes
use_cases.description: Document container interfaces, protocols, dependencies, and API specifications before implementation review.

use_cases.title: Review deployment boundaries
use_cases.description: Compare containers, databases, queues, and external systems in a shared C4 model view.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first container draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a small service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create C4 container-level documentation for this system. Use my component list, technologies, and deployment notes. Include containers, interfaces, dependencies, and a Mermaid diagram outline.

prompt_templates.title: Map components into containers
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for existing component documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these component documents and group them into deployment containers. Explain each boundary, list contained components, and identify missing deployment details.

prompt_templates.title: Document interfaces and dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for API and integration review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create container interface documentation from these service notes. Include protocols, endpoints, external systems, dependencies, and OpenAPI specification guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize a complete C4 package
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a complete C4 container package from these component, API, infrastructure, and deployment inputs. Include rationale, diagrams, API summaries, scaling notes, and review gaps.

output_examples.input: A web app, API service, PostgreSQL database, and message queue with brief component notes.
output: A container summary with web, API, database, and queue responsibilities.
A dependency list that explains user, service, database, and messaging relationships.
A Mermaid C4Container diagram outline for the deployment view.

output_examples.input: Several component documents and a Kubernetes deployment summary for a microservice system.
output: A mapped list of components inside each deployment container.
An interface summary with REST, event, and database interactions.
A gap list for missing scaling, resource, and ownership details.

output_examples.input: API notes for a container that exposes public and internal endpoints.
output: A container API section with protocol, purpose, endpoint groups, and consumers.
OpenAPI specification guidance for request parameters and response descriptions.
Dependencies and external systems that should appear on the container diagram.

best_practices: Provide component documents, deployment notes, and known infrastructure constraints together.
Keep container names aligned with real deployable units and ownership boundaries.
Review generated diagrams with engineers who operate the services.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for code-level class or function documentation.
Do not invent containers when deployment ownership is unknown.
Do not treat placeholder OpenAPI examples as production specifications.

faq.question: What C4 level does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on the Container level, where deployable units, data stores, queues, and external systems are documented.

faq.question: Can it create Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides Mermaid C4Container diagram structure for container-level architecture views.

faq.question: Does it validate OpenAPI specifications?
faq.answer: No. It provides API documentation guidance, but a separate validator should check OpenAPI syntax.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Use component documents, service names, deployment notes, API summaries, dependencies, and infrastructure constraints.

faq.question: Is this useful for microservices?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful when services, databases, queues, and external integrations need a shared deployment view.

faq.question: Can it replace architecture review?
faq.answer: No. It prepares consistent documentation that architects and service owners can review.
